items.title: Medication safety
reviewers: Clinical SME — medication record checks and escalation responsibilities
Andrew, Senior Learning Designer — fit of the reference for the intended learning activity
items.html:
Purpose and scope

Use this reference when checking medication information and handing responsibility to another member of the care team.

Check the record

  • Confirm the patient’s identity using the local identification procedure.
  • Check the current medication list, allergies and documented adverse reactions.
  • If information is missing or conflicts with another record, ask the supervising clinician or pharmacist to reconcile it before relying on it.

Communicate changes

Record discrepancies, who was contacted and the agreed follow-up. At a transition of care, pass the current list and outstanding questions to the receiving clinician. Use the incident reporting process for a medication incident or near miss.

Further reading

  • Medication Safety Standard

items.title: Nursing and clinical handover
reviewers: Nursing SME — clinical handover content and transfer of responsibility
Andrew, Senior Learning Designer — whether the handover task elicits the evidence expected for the unit
items.html:
Prepare the handover

Identify the patient using the local identification procedure. Check the record, ask about the patient’s priorities and gather the latest relevant observations.

Give the handover

  1. Introduce yourself and identify the colleague receiving the handover.
  2. Describe the current situation, relevant background and changes since the last handover. Distinguish observations from information that still needs checking.
  3. Explain each outstanding action, who is responsible and when it needs attention.

Close the loop

Invite questions. Ask the receiving colleague to confirm the next action and who will take it. Document the transfer of responsibility and any unresolved concerns in the patient record.

Further reading

  • Communicating for Safety Standard

items.title: Booking an interpreter
reviewers: Interpreting SME — booking steps and the local confirmation and follow-up process
items.reason: The original page contained an unfilled policy template
items.html:
Ask about communication needs

Ask the person which language and dialect they prefer and whether they have a preference relevant to the booking. Record their answer and the support requested.

Prepare the booking

Gather the appointment date, time, duration, location or remote format, and purpose. Use the language service’s booking channel. Share only the details needed to arrange the service.

Track the request

Record when the request was made, who will follow up and which details are outstanding. Once the service confirms the booking, record the confirmation and tell the person and appointment team.

Before the appointment

Check the room or remote connection, allow time for briefing, and introduce the interpreter and their role. Speak directly to the person and allow time for questions.

Further reading

  • Arranging an interpreter
  • Preparing for interpreting

items.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander liaison services
reviewers: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander liaison or cultural safety reviewer — cultural wording, service scope and local referral arrangements
items.reason: The source service page was unavailable. The archived directory identifies four liaison staff. Referral arrangements, hours and reporting lines still need confirmation.
items.html:
Requesting liaison support

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients and families can choose whether they would like liaison support. Ask the person who they want involved, what help they would like and what they are comfortable sharing with the team.

Prepare the handover

With the person’s agreement, record their request in their own words, the people they want included, any communication preferences and the best way to follow up. Agree who will update them about the request.

items.title: Laboratory PPE reference
reviewers: Laboratory safety SME — task-specific protective equipment guidance
items.reason: Replace the archived drag activity with an appropriate intranet reference and separate practice
items.html:
Start with the task

Check the task risk assessment and local procedure to identify the required protective equipment. Different tasks can require different protection.

Before work

  • Check the required protective clothing, hand and eye protection, and footwear.
  • Check the equipment fits and is in good condition.
  • Ask the supervisor to clarify missing instructions or arrange suitable equipment before starting the task.

items.title: Laboratory waste reference
reviewers: Laboratory safety and waste SME — local waste classifications and handling guidance
items.reason: The archived answer key categorised unspecified expired medication as cytotoxic waste
items.html:
Identify the material

Check what the material is, what it has been used for and what it may be contaminated with. Use the local waste procedure and the label on the designated container to confirm the waste stream.

If the waste stream is unclear

Leave the item where it can be managed safely and ask the supervisor how to proceed. The appearance of an item or the colour of a container does not establish the correct waste stream. For an expired medicine, identify the medicine before deciding how it should be managed.
